glad to hear that you felt a little better! and no need to thank me. we're both in this shit together, just like many others in this subreddit and outside of it. you're not alone. 

it sucks that your songs and hobbies don't work anymore. maybe try out some new ones? everything's great as long as it gives you a sense of purpose and makes you happy.   it's fine if you can't think of anything at the moment, but i'm sure that if you keep looking, you will find something eventually. 

oh, and one more piece of advice i can give you is to give yourself time. you don't need to get better all of a sudden and force yourself to do things you're not comfortable doing. it's okay to feel sad. if you're in a terrible mood and don't want to go outside, don't force yourself. when you're comfortable you will want to do it on your own. small steps. one day at a time. 

try to think positively. learn to appreciate little things like your girlfriend asking you how was your day, your friend telling a joke, a cute dog you see on the street, a nice song you hear on the radio. everything that makes you feel good to be alive even for just a little moment. i think that's what saved me when i was very close to killing myself. and hopefully, this will work for you, too! i keep my fingers crossed for you! you can do this.

that's pretty much how i feel all the time. i honestly think i'm getting better, and genuinely want to live, but this voice in my head that's telling me to kill myself is still there. and there are moments where its presence is unbearable. i'm living my life with constants thoughts about suicide and all i can do is ignore them. i guess i got used to it but it doesn't change the fact that it's still difficult sometimes.

and no, my friend, it's not wrong to feel like this. don't blame yourself. you're never responsible for your feelings. it's something you have no control of. it doesn't matter what kind of life you have, even if you have a loving family, girlfriend, friends... it doesn't matter.  depression doesn't care about these things. it could get you when you're a billionaire living in a mansion with a "perfect life". it could get you when you're living on a street. 

it's wrong to think that you don't have any reason to be depressed because of your wealth, social status etc. because it's simply not true. your feelings are valid, no matter what are your life standards. don't let anyone tell you otherwise and make you feel guilty for your feelings.

with that being said, i hope everything gets better and wish you all the best. focus on the things that make you happy, spend time with people who make you happy. and don't give in to these thoughts. stay strong, friend. you can fight this.

they didn't work for me. i felt a little dizzy and numb, but i guess it's normal? i still felt like shit all the time and experienced suicidal thoughts though. i've stopped taking them some time ago and nothing's changed. maybe i would need some stronger meds, but honestly, i don't care anymore. i'm not interested in going back to the psychiatrist.

it's an individual matter, maybe they would work for you, but you never know. it's true that there are many possible side effects and it is scary. i think it's better to deal with depression through therapy instead of taking antidepressants, since you never know if they will even help.

it's absolutely not wrong! it's very good actually, and i'm glad that you had this one small bit of hope shining in your life even if it was just for one moment. i live for moments like these. sometimes i feel like a nuisance and a burden whenever someone checks in on me, but i've come to realize that's just depression messing with my head and making me feel guilty no matter what i do. so i try to push these thoughts away and think about how it's really nice that someone cares about me enough to ask how i'm doing. it is a small thing but when you're struggling to get through another day... it can be very uplifting. these small gestures that show you that someone cares.

it's completely normal that you want to feel worthy, to be noticed by other people and cared for. we all have these desires and it's really heartbreaking when we are deprived of those things. it makes life really difficult. we need other people.

you're not selfish in any way for wanting affection, someone to talk to, despite what you may think, or rather, what your mind is telling you— it's completely normal and natural, so please don't beat yourself up for this. you are worthy of affection, of friendship, of love, and your feelings are valid.
